comparisons.peer_topic: Data center and cloud computing solutions
comparisons.peer_summary: The company offers a deep portfolio of data center solutions including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, SmartNICs, and FPGAs to meet performance requirements for data centers, supercomputers, and cloud environments.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD describe providing comprehensive, end-to-end hardware platforms for AI workloads that encompass multiple processing unit types. NVIDIA emphasizes its 'complete, end-to-end accelerated computing platform' including GPUs, CPUs, and DPUs for both training and inferencing. Similarly, AMD highlights a 'deep portfolio of data center computing solutions' that includes AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, and DPUs to meet the performance requirements of AI and ML environments. Both companies position themselves as providers of multi-component silicon solutions rather than single-product vendors.

sentences.text: We provide a complete, end-to-end accelerated computing platform for AI, addressing both training and inferencing.
Our compute solutions include all three major processing units in AI servers - GPUs, CPUs, and DPUs.

We offer a deep portfolio of data center computing solutions including AI accelerators, microprocessors (CPUs), graphic processing units (GPUs), data processing units (DPUs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs), and field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), to meet the vast computing performance requirements of today's data centers, supercomputers, AI and Machine Learning (ML) data center environments and cloud environments.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD completed the acquisition of Silo AI in 2024, expanding its AI model development capabilities and gaining a software stack for training large language models on AMD Instinct accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: While NVIDIA describes its software leadership through its own NeMo platform and developer ecosystem, AMD expanded its AI capabilities through the acquisition of Silo AI to strengthen its model development and software stack for LLMs. Both disclosures highlight efforts to enhance software infrastructure for training large language models, but NVIDIA focuses on its proprietary tools (NeMo) and ecosystem scale, whereas AMD focused on acquiring external expertise to build its training solutions.

sentences.text: In addition, we offer DGX Cloud, an AI-training-as-a-service platform, and NeMo - a complete solution for building enterprise-ready Large Language Models, or LLMs, using open source and proprietary LLMs created by NVIDIA and third parties.
Our AI technology leadership is reinforced by our large and expanding ecosystem in a virtuous cycle.
During the year, we completed the acquisition of Silo AI Oy (Silo AI), an AI lab based in Finland.

Silo AI has also developed a software stack used to train multiple state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs) on AMD Instinct accelerators that can accelerate the development of highly-performant AMD training solutions.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates for AVGO (avgo_2024_1_D069 and avgo_2024_1_D034) focus on enterprise software distribution, VMware infrastructure, and Tanzu application platforms. These do not substantively overlap with NVIDIA's disclosure of hardware-centric AI accelerated computing platforms (GPUs, DPUs) or its specific developer ecosystem for AI training/inferencing.

comparisons.peer_topic: Software strategy and open source contributions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel aims to optimize AI frameworks and maintains the OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference. In 2024, Intel launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation and contributed oneAPI specifications to the UXL Foundation to enable open, multi-vendor programming across accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Intel emphasize the importance of software ecosystems and frameworks to support their AI hardware. NVIDIA highlights its 'NeMo' solution and 'large and expanding ecosystem' of developers using CUDA. Intel focuses on optimizing AI frameworks (like PyTorch, TensorFlow) on its hardware and launching open standards like 'oneAPI' to enable cross-architecture development. While NVIDIA leverages a proprietary, tightly integrated ecosystem, Intel promotes open, multi-vendor interoperability through oneAPI and industry foundations.

sentences.text: In addition, we offer DGX Cloud, an AI-training-as-a-service platform, and NeMo - a complete solution for building enterprise-ready Large Language Models, or LLMs, using open source and proprietary LLMs created by NVIDIA and third parties.
Our AI technology leadership is reinforced by our large and expanding ecosystem in a virtuous cycle.
We aim to optimize AI frameworks and middleware, such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, vLLM, Hugging Face and WebNN to run efficiently on our hardware.

Most of these frameworks and middleware are built from our oneAPI, which enables developers to create performant cross-architecture applications using a single code base across CPUs, GPUs, and other accelerators.

comparisons.peer_summary: CNBU data center sales were driven by server demand in cloud and enterprise markets, with growth fueled by the shift of infrastructure and workloads to the cloud and the memory-intensive nature of AI data-centric workloads.
comparisons.comparison: NVIDIA’s disclosure of providing a complete platform for AI training and inferencing implies a heavy reliance on memory-intensive workloads, which aligns with Micron's explicit statement that cloud servers supporting AI and data-centric workloads require 'significantly increasing quantities of DRAM, including HBM.' Both disclosures reflect the same underlying business driver: the surge in AI data-centric workloads demanding high-performance memory solutions.

sentences.text: We provide a complete, end-to-end accelerated computing platform for AI, addressing both training and inferencing.

Cloud servers supporting AI and data-centric workloads require significantly increasing quantities of DRAM, including HBM, and NAND as the task of turning data into insight becomes increasingly memory-centric.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates for QCOM (qcom_2024_1_D029 and qcom_2024_1_D049) focus on on-device AI inference (edge/mobile) via the Snapdragon AI Engine and R&D diversification into automotive/IoT. This differs fundamentally from NVIDIA's disclosure of large-scale data center AI training and inferencing platforms.
